stemMd: A shop tests a new display for one week and sales rise. The week also includes a major festival that brings many extra visitors. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.label: B
options.textMd: The sales rise alone does not isolate the display’s effect.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The display certainly caused the entire rise.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The festival had no possible influence.

options.label: E
options.textMd: No future test of displays could ever be informative.

explanationMd: The display change and festival occurred together. Increased visitor traffic could explain some or all of the sales rise, so the observation does not isolate the display’s contribution. The proper conclusion is uncertainty about attribution, not proof of no effect.

distractorRationale.a: The data do not establish a negative effect.
distractorRationale.d: Extra visitors provide a plausible alternative cause.
distractorRationale.c: The simultaneous festival prevents that attribution.
distractorRationale.e: A better-controlled comparison could be useful.
